name: Verath & Lund Birdseye Sweater
description:
A crewneck sweater knitted in a traditional birdseye pattern — small, repeating two-color diamond checks — from Verath & Lund's house merino-cashmere blend. The yarn is sourced from a cooperative in what was once Patagonia and processed at V&L's mill in the upper Great Lakes corridor. The result is a sweater with genuine weight and presence: it holds its shape, repels light moisture, and softens over time rather than pilling. Colors come in pairs — the birdseye is always two tones, typically a neutral ground with a darker check, or occasionally an unexpected pairing like sage and burgundy.

Verath & Lund occupies a strange position in GLMZ's fashion landscape — they're not fashionable, exactly, but they are respected. The Birdseye Sweater is something a Tier 3 professional might inherit from a parent or save up for deliberately, wear for fifteen years, and eventually hand off again. It sits equally well in a Tier 3 apartment and at a Tier 4 casual gathering. It is the sweater of people who buy things once.
what_it_says: You buy quality and you keep it. There's a quiet confidence here — not display, not restraint for its own sake, just someone who knows what they like and has had time to acquire it.
story_hooks: Verath & Lund's Patagonian yarn cooperative is in a dispute with an Ouroboros agricultural subsidiary that wants the land — the mill is quietly lobbying GLMZ's city council, and a character might get drawn into the politics.

A specific colorway of the Birdseye Sweater — slate ground, rust check — was worn by a prominent whistleblower in their most-circulated photograph; wearing one now reads as a political statement in some circles.
A character finds a V&L Birdseye in a dead drop alongside an encoded message, the sweater's pattern itself used as a cipher key.
